items.title: [agfundernews.com] John Deere buys Orchard AI to add plant-level crop data
items.content_html: John Deere has acquired Orchard Robotics, which operates as Orchard AI, adding its camera-based crop monitoring and FruitScope software to the equipment maker’s precision-agriculture business. The deal, announced Nov. 19, pairs plant-level data for specialty-crop growers with Deere machinery that can act on field recommendations. Financial terms were not disclosed. The system scans trees, vines and other crops to assess fruit size, crop health and expected yield, helping growers decide when and where to thin, spray or harvest. Orchard will remain a Deere subsidiary with its existing team and products, founder and CEO Charlie Wu said. The acquisition also expands Deere’s orchard and vineyard automation portfolio.

items.title: [agro-tv.ro] Romanian veterinary authority intensifies sheep pox vaccination drive to restore exports
items.content_html: Romania’s National Sanitary Veterinary and Food Safety Authority (ANSVSA) has stepped up coordination of the compulsory vaccination campaign against sheep and goat pox. Authority president Alexandru Nicolae Bociu convened a meeting with county veterinary offices on Nov. 19. The campaign aims to protect flocks and help resume exports of sheep and goats. ANSVSA says vaccination is free and it will monitor the campaign centrally each day, with weekly reviews of progress in each county. It also plans to report campaign developments to the European Commission. The authority says milk and meat from vaccinated animals can be consumed without vaccine-related restrictions.

items.title: [dagenslantbruk.se] Farmers and agribusinesses test AI to cut costs and improve crops
items.content_html: Agricultural companies, researchers and farmers are using artificial intelligence for crop monitoring, breeding, irrigation and farm administration, as tools move from research into field trials. A survey previewed at the PLUSAGRI 2026 conference in Warsaw on Nov. 18 found that 53.9% of participating Polish farmers said they use AI; organizers planned to present findings on how farmers use the technology and how much they trust it. Sweden’s Lantmännen says it uses AI in plant breeding and to improve the use of fertilizer, crop protection products and water. Applications range from software that analyzes crop images and farm data to AI-guided irrigation. A European potato program supported by Cropin examined how farming practices affect water use and potato quality, while researchers have reported AI systems that identify crop models from agricultural data. A Chinese provincial study analyzed data from 2005 to 2023, while newer tools still require testing across crops and climates before broader use.

items.title: [hurriyetdailynews.com] World Bank unveils $6.9 billion climate investment package at COP31
items.content_html: The World Bank Group announced more than $6.9 billion in climate and development investments at the COP31 summit in Antalya on Nov. 17. The package is expected to mobilize $10.7 billion in private capital across agriculture, manufacturing, infrastructure and renewable energy. In Türkiye, an agricultural operation aims to expand farmers’ access to finance and markets, strengthen supply chains and help cut emissions from production. It is expected to benefit 225,000 farmers and support more than 100,000 job equivalents. The package also includes support for an organic fertilizer plant in Afghanistan that would turn agricultural waste into locally produced farm inputs. Its stated aims are to improve soil health and farm productivity and create jobs.
